feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope of responsibility is consistently impressive. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director to consultant, which reinforces credibility and growth.  
- Good domain specificity: Drupal, analytics stack, AI search, governance, and multimedia capabilities make the profile concrete and differentiated.  
- Effective use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and newsletter reach add impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more results language: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “developed,” “advised”) without showing measurable outcomes such as engagement gains, efficiency improvements, or campaign performance.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around list items is inconsistent; use either “social media and video” or “social, and multimedia” consistently; “A2/Learning” would read more cleanly as “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value statement plus one scope sentence; foreground public-sector digital transformation and team/operating model leadership.
- Add 1–2 concrete signals of scale or complexity from recent roles (for example, enterprise web modernization, 10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views).
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct action verbs like “leading,” “modernizing,” or “scaling.”
- Consider rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading public-sector web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for complex, mission-driven organizations. Oversees enterprise platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences supporting high-volume communications at scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; use the intro to add scale/results instead.
- The capability list repeats core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership scope will make it feel more distinctive and executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Replace vague or repetitive terms with sharper, broader ones: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”; “Workflow automation and platform integrations” instead of singular “integration”
- Consider prioritizing most senior/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, then communications and multimedia
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search…” repeat language from the header and recent projects
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps with Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several points already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line and format as concise, parallel bullets or mini case studies for easier scanning.
- Tighten wording: “AI-enabled legislative search combining hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Make each project more outcome- or purpose-led, e.g., “to improve policy discovery,” “to support campaign growth,” “to extend conference engagement.”
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo experience bullets; keep this section focused on standout examples, not restating responsibilities.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all entries; vary verbs or use a consistent noun-led format.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around 3–4 outcomes-focused themes and avoid repeating NACo achievements already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, campaign delivery and content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper impact statements: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving coordination and publishing efficiency.
- Rephrase technical work to emphasize outcomes, not tasks: “Built Drupal-based campaign experiences and reusable content modules that streamlined launches and improved member resource discovery.”
- Add measurable results where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, toolkit downloads, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media entry on governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement.
- Microsites and AI search also duplicate the Recent Projects section; mention them briefly here, but keep project detail there.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, deliverability, or campaign impact metrics for email/social if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets to action + result: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy and event programming”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems-building.
- Video-programming language also echoes earlier roles; emphasize studio buildout and operational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge position than a distinct achievement-based role. Tighten it to emphasize what was owned and what expanded during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger verbs and specifics: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video” and “weekly updates” also appear in the prior role and footer project list; avoid repeating production details unless you add a distinct result.
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the Director role; keep this version focused on execution rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current differentiators from recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused content planning” beside broader leadership terms.
- If space allows, make one item more distinctive to recent work, e.g. “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” or “Digital governance for 10,000+ page platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already well established in the summary and work history; keep only if other skills are trimmed elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize recent strengths tied to Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” is stronger than listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths; move Drupal, AI-enabled search, workflow automation, and API integrations to the front.
- Trim lower-signal or dated items here (for example jQuery) since detailed tools already appear elsewhere.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • AI-enabled search experiences • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable systems • WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep this section high-level and let the later section carry the full tool inventory.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; use wording here that is more execution-focused.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization” rather than just product names.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for sharper wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid listing every tool here if they already appear in Technical + IT; keep this section more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership impact rather than listing basic functions.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider replacing “video production and editing” with “broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the in-house studio build and seniority.
- Use parallel, concise phrasing; avoid mixing broad categories (“studio operations”) with narrow tools (“PTZ camera systems”) unless all bullets are similarly scoped.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to outcomes in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., built in-house studio, expanded advocacy programming, supported recurring livestreams).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- Tool-level detail here also overlaps with Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows,” Premiere Pro, Audition).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same message.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and consider dropping the least relevant one if space is tight: Drupal should clearly lead given recent NACo work.
- If you want more impact, rename the item to “CMS Platforms” and add a light qualifier such as “enterprise, campaign and intranet environments.”
- Keep formatting parallel; avoid mixing platform names here with broader capabilities already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages is not reinforced elsewhere; keep it only if it supports a specific project or portfolio use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add specificity that signals level: e.g., “custom front-end components,” “third-party/API integrations,” or “CI/CD workflow automation.”
- Order by strongest/most distinctive tools first: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, API integrations, then HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under Analytics/Data rather than Coding & Technical Implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Remove lower-value/general tools unless they were central in recent roles: Basecamp and Trello are less important given your senior, enterprise-focused profile.
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use “Microsoft Teams,” not “Teams.”
- If accurate, add a light proficiency cue in the heading or formatting, e.g., “Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable (system design), Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; this section should stay tool-specific, not repeat capability language.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are partially redundant as project-management variants; listing all four dilutes impact.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and doesn’t show level of ownership or enterprise context. Since recent roles emphasize email operations, frame these as platforms used to run member communications and engagement at scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member engagement workflows)**
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: **…supporting newsletters and campaigns reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders**
- Keep platform names only if space is tight; otherwise add a short functional qualifier so this reads as capability, not just software.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating audience scale here unless the experience bullets stay outcome-focused.
- “Engagement” may blur with social/community work; “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” is clearer and more specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” plus the Director role. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack entry and emphasize methods over broad concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI/dashboard reporting** to sound more outcome-oriented and less vague.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity**.
- If space allows elsewhere, move impact to experience bullets instead of here (e.g., reporting adoption, decision-making improvements, testing wins).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider deleting one version or making this one strictly tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the **Director of Digital Media** entry, so avoid adding narrative here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and video operations.”
- Add concrete contributions and scale where possible: website refresh, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, event coverage, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating: “Mentored a digital media associate and helped standardize day-to-day publishing and production workflows.”
- Possible full rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media function. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and multimedia while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in 2022–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work at NACo. It should be tightened and framed around distinctive contributions—especially the first podcast—without repeating digital/media themes covered more strongly in later roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the most unique, resume-worthy achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope or audience, e.g., “supported county-focused research and innovation initiatives for program and policy teams.”
- Keep multimedia mention concise and action-oriented: “produced digital and multimedia content” rather than “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Supported county-focused research and innovation initiatives for NACo’s program and policy teams. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production, and produced supporting digital and multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing broad digital content production; later NACo roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership in much stronger terms.
- If possible, add one concrete output or result for the podcast/research work to differentiate this entry.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it currently mixes software with production capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it to tool-specific terms will make it cleaner and less redundant.

Suggested edit:
- Separate tools from capabilities; keep this line focused on named platforms/software.
